title: Southeast Asia: Rice Ferments, Palm Toddy & Their Spirits
attribution: Southeast Asia ferments glutinous rice and palm sap with mixed-mould starter cakes (ragi/bubod/loog-pang) into a spectrum of sweet pastes, cloudy wines and clear distillates. Mostly traditional with little statutory definition; lambanog and some rice wines are commercially produced. Documented from ethnographic and food-science sources; values are typical.

styles.name: Tapai / Tapuy (Fermented Rice)
styles.impression: Sweet, sour and lightly alcoholic fermented glutinous rice (or cassava) — eaten as a dessert paste or drunk as it liquefies into rice wine.
styles.comments: Tapai ubi (cassava) and tapai pulut (rice) across Malaysia/Indonesia; tapuy in the Philippines. The liquid that collects is the rice wine; the solids are eaten. A close analogue to the Chinese jiuniang.
styles.ingredients: Steamed glutinous rice (or cassava) inoculated with ragi/bubod — a starter cake of Amylomyces mould and yeast that saccharifies and ferments at once.
styles.tags: seasia, tapai, tapuy, ragi, rice, traditional

styles.name: Brem / Rice Wine (Bali)
styles.impression: Balinese fermented glutinous (often black) rice wine — sweet, reddish-brown, low-to-moderate strength, used in offering and refreshment.
styles.comments: Brem Bali is bottled commercially. A solid brem cake is also sold as a snack.
styles.ingredients: Black or white glutinous rice fermented with ragi tapai starter; the liquid is aged.

styles.name: Sato / Lao Hai / Rice Wine of the Mekong
styles.impression: Thai and Lao fermented sticky-rice wine — sweet-sour and cloudy, the sipped 'jar wine' drunk communally through long reeds from a fermentation pot.
styles.comments: Sato is the Thai bottled version; lao hai is the communal jar. A parallel to Himalayan tongba and chhaang.
styles.ingredients: Steamed glutinous rice with loog-pang (Thai) or similar starter, fermented in a jar; water is added and the wine sipped through bamboo straws (lao hai).
styles.tags: thailand, laos, sato, rice-wine, jar-wine, traditional

styles.name: Tuba (Palm Toddy)
styles.impression: Philippine and Southeast Asian coconut palm toddy — sweet and fresh when tapped, souring through the day; sometimes reddened with barok (mangrove bark tannin).
styles.comments: Widespread across the Philippines and the Pacific. Aged tuba becomes vinegar (suka); distilled it becomes lambanog.
styles.ingredients: Coconut palm sap, wild-fermented; barok bark may be added for colour, tannin and preservation.

styles.name: Lambanog (Coconut Arrack)
styles.impression: The Philippine 'coconut vodka' — a clear, potent distillate of coconut toddy, smooth and neutral to fruity, now bottled in flavoured commercial lines.
styles.comments: A regional craft spirit of Quezon province, increasingly exported. Traditionally sold in recycled bottles at rural markets.
styles.ingredients: Fermented coconut toddy (tuba), pot-distilled, sometimes twice.
